# m5 contact sheet
# Part 2 of 2 (m5-contact-sheet-1.txt … m5-contact-sheet-2.txt), each at most 180 000 B.
#
# Promise: you see the result before you confirm — the ghost the preview draws is what git then does, and u takes it back (TESTING.md "History").
#
# Generated by scripts/contact-sheet.sh — do not hand-edit; edit
# m5-contact-sheet-captions.tsv and re-run instead.
#
# 62 captures in all, in ticket order.
#
# These are character-grid captures (pyte/TestBackend), not pixels:
# colour is never verifiable from this file. Judge colour only in a
# real terminal, never from a capture (CLAUDE.md rule 5).
#
# Scroll once: each capture is delimited by a heading naming its
# file (docs/shots/<name>) and what right looks like for it.

docs/shots/m5-ui-confirm-over-graph-160x48.txt
what right looks like: Capture header "What right looks like here" (ADR-0040): the push-confirm box does not clear its band — the graph rows beside it stay visible — and every surviving column is whole: the box's edges snap to row-column boundaries so there's a blank gutter column between border and SHA rather than them reading as one token, with no clipped subject and no four-character SHA tail. On the widest surviving row `●` sits left of the border and `GF 2d   c8254c5` sits right of it.
================================================================================

# m5-ui-confirm-over-graph-160x48.txt: 160x48, drawn by
# `view::view` from a real AppState — the Linear corpus cloned into a
# `file://` bare, the clone left one commit ahead of it, the walk let
# settle, then `P` pressed
# (crates/graft/tests/it/two_boxes_over_content.rs,
# capture_two_boxes_over_real_content_for_docs_shots, asserted).
# Not a pty capture: the terminal is ratatui's TestBackend, so this is
# a character grid with no colour attributes in it — CLAUDE.md rule 5,
# colour ships unverified. The scratch repository's temporary path is
# set to `/code/api` and the clock to the corpus's own `now` **before**
# the frame is drawn, so the header is laid out against the width a
# real checkout takes and the ages never move.
#
# **What right looks like here** (ADR-0040): the box does **not**
# clear its band — the rows beside it are the graph you are about to
# act on, and seeing them is M5's promise. Instead every column that
# survives beside it survives **whole**: its left edge sits on a
# boundary between two row columns and its right edge one cell short
# of one, on that column's **gutter**, so there is a blank column
# between the border and the SHA rather than `╮60af0eb` reading as one
# token (ADR-0040's 2026-09-21 amendment). No clipped subject, no
# four-character tail of a SHA. The box's content is never shrunk to
# reach a position; if none fitted, it would clear instead — though
# the gutter costs the box a cell, and at 80 columns that is the cell
# its longest line used as right-hand padding. Judge that by eye.
#
# The snap is computed where the screen is laid out
# (`graft::view::frame`, from `GraphScreen::column_boundaries`), not
# inside the widget — ADR-0040 clause 3, so the box stays a box and
# knows nothing about the graph.
#
# What is behind it: 200 commits of ordinary history, the tip one
# commit ahead of `origin/main`, with the graph filling the rows
# above, below and beside the frame.
#
# What survives beside it, read back out of the frame below rather
# than written here by hand — on the widest such row, `●` is
# left of the border and `GF 2d   c8254c5` is right of it.
#
# The 3-choice box `u` opens once the work is on a remote (ADR-0038
# §4) stands on this same corpus and is in
# docs/shots/m5-ui-undo-after-push-80x24.txt. It is not reproduced
# here: reaching it needs a commit Graft makes **during** the run,
# and git stamps that commit from the wall clock, so its oid — which
# the box and the header both draw — would move every run and this
# file could not be diffed.

== `P`: the push confirm, on the graph ==

# docs/shots/m5-ui-conflicts.txt — CONFLICTS section, changes pane
#
# What right looks like: `CONFLICTS (n)` heads the file list, ahead
# of Staged/Unstaged/Untracked. Its row shows the porcelain pair as
# words (`both modified`) in the trailing column, never a single
# letter and add/remove counts — there is no single "the diff"
# while both sides are still in the index.

docs/shots/m5-ui-context-menu-verbs-160x48.txt
what right looks like: Capture header "What right looks like": the same context menu — `Checkout main` then `Cherry-pick <sha7>` first (since m6-conflicts/71), then the row's own actions, then the rest of the history verbs naming real branches (`Merge main into feature (m)`, `Rebase feature onto main (r)`, `Reset feature to here, mixed`/`, hard`, `Delete branch main`), then ambient verbs, rows opaque, trailing `(key)` only where live. At 160 columns the graph's date and sha columns sit far right of the menu and stop dead at its rows, so no verb has a stray sha beside it.
================================================================================

# m5-ui-context-menu-verbs-160x48.txt: 160x48, drawn by `view::view`
# from a real AppState — a real repository (`main` three commits, `feature`
# forked off the first with two of its own, `feature` checked out), opened
# over the real job pool, cursor moved to `main`'s row and `.` pressed
# through `update`
# (crates/graft/tests/it/context_menu.rs, capture_context_menu_for_docs_shots).
# This file is a golden snapshot: that test asserts the frame still
# matches it, so drift fails the suite. Regenerate on purpose with
# GRAFT_UPDATE_SHOTS=1. Not a pty capture: the terminal is ratatui's
# TestBackend, so this is a character grid with no colour attributes in
# it — CLAUDE.md rule 5, colour ships unverified. The fixture's commits
# carry fixed dates and the ages are drawn against a fixed clock, so the
# frame is the same on every run and does not age. The repository is
# moved to `/code/api` **before** the frame is drawn, so the header is
# fitted to the path shown here rather than to a temporary one, and the
# walk's sort and the radar have landed — a settled screen, not a transient.
#
# What right looks like:
#  - The menu is anchored under `main`'s row and is wide enough for its
#    longest label, with the cursor on the first item.
#  - `Checkout main` then `Cherry-pick <sha7> (o)` come first (m6-conflicts/71),
#    then `Explain` if the row is marked, then the row's own actions
#    (`Copy SHA (y)`, `Compare with this (x)`, `Open details (⏎)`),
#    then the rest of the history verbs, then the ambient
#    ones (`Fetch (f)` … `Undo (u)`). The menu lists every verb valid for
#    this row at every width — it does not filter against the hint bar,
#    because a verb you can only discover at 160 columns is the failure
#    ADR-0039 exists to prevent.
#  - The menu is opaque. On each of its rows, everything right of the
#    label is blank out to the edge of the pane: no date or sha from the
#    commit row underneath survives beside a verb, where it would read as
#    if the verb were bound to that sha.
#  - The history verbs name the real branches, not placeholders: `Checkout
#    main`, `Merge main into feature (m)`, `Rebase feature onto main (r)`,
#    `Cherry-pick <sha7> (o)`, `Revert <sha7>`, `Reset feature to here,
#    mixed`/`, hard`, `Delete branch main`. `feature` is the branch
#    checked out, `main` is the row under the cursor.
#  - No verb names the branch you are standing on where git would refuse
#    it: there is no `Checkout feature` and no `Delete branch feature`.
#  - A trailing `(key)` means one thing everywhere in the menu: that
#    letter is live right now, so next time you can skip the menu. Only
#    `Merge`, `Rebase` and `Cherry-pick` carry one, because only `m`, `r`
#    and `o` (M7) exist. A
#    qualifier that is not a key never wears that shape — hence `Reset
#    …, mixed`, not `(mixed)` (`docs/design/02-keymap.md` §2.1).
#  - Choosing any of them opens a picture, not a write (PROMPT.md §1.7).
#  - The marker column has settled: `feature`'s tip carries the radar's
#    muted `ⓘ`. Earlier captures were taken before the radar
#    answered and the column was blank — that was the transient, not
#    this. What the finding says is not part of this picture.
#  - At 160 columns the graph's date and sha columns sit far to the
#    right of the menu, and they stop dead at the menu's own rows: the
#    popup clears the whole band it stands on, so no verb has a stray
#    sha beside it.
#

 graft /code/api  8 commits
  ◆    [◆ feature] finish the feature                                                                                                            GF now  8d6cd28
  ●    start the feature                                                                                                                         GF 2m   52f3b96
● │ ▏  [main] main moves again                                                                                                                   GF 3m   45fa51d

docs/shots/m5-ui-context-menu-verbs-80x24.txt
what right looks like: Capture header "What right looks like": the context menu anchors under the clicked row, cursor on the first item, leading with `Checkout main` then `Cherry-pick <sha7>` (since m6-conflicts/71), then the row's own actions (`Copy SHA (y)`, `Compare with this (x)`, `Open details (⏎)`), then the rest of the history verbs naming the real branches (`Merge main into feature (m)`, `Rebase feature onto main (r)`, `Revert <sha7>`, `Reset feature to here, mixed`/`, hard`, `Delete branch main`), then ambient verbs — never naming the checked-out branch where git would refuse it. Rows are opaque, a trailing `(key)` appears only where that key is live (`m`, `r`), and at 80 columns the menu still fits inside the graph pane.
================================================================================

# m5-ui-context-menu-verbs-80x24.txt: 80x24, drawn by `view::view`
# from a real AppState — a real repository (`main` three commits, `feature`
# forked off the first with two of its own, `feature` checked out), opened
# over the real job pool, cursor moved to `main`'s row and `.` pressed
# through `update`
# (crates/graft/tests/it/context_menu.rs, capture_context_menu_for_docs_shots).
# This file is a golden snapshot: that test asserts the frame still
# matches it, so drift fails the suite. Regenerate on purpose with
# GRAFT_UPDATE_SHOTS=1. Not a pty capture: the terminal is ratatui's
# TestBackend, so this is a character grid with no colour attributes in
# it — CLAUDE.md rule 5, colour ships unverified. The fixture's commits
# carry fixed dates and the ages are drawn against a fixed clock, so the
# frame is the same on every run and does not age. The repository is
# moved to `/code/api` **before** the frame is drawn, so the header is
# fitted to the path shown here rather than to a temporary one, and the
# walk's sort and the radar have landed — a settled screen, not a transient.
#
# What right looks like:
#  - The menu is anchored under `main`'s row and is wide enough for its
#    longest label, with the cursor on the first item.
#  - `Checkout main` then `Cherry-pick <sha7> (o)` come first (m6-conflicts/71),
#    then `Explain` if the row is marked, then the row's own actions
#    (`Copy SHA (y)`, `Compare with this (x)`, `Open details (⏎)`),
#    then the rest of the history verbs, then the ambient
#    ones (`Fetch (f)` … `Undo (u)`). The menu lists every verb valid for
#    this row at every width — it does not filter against the hint bar,
#    because a verb you can only discover at 160 columns is the failure
#    ADR-0039 exists to prevent.
#  - The menu is opaque. On each of its rows, everything right of the
#    label is blank out to the edge of the pane: no date or sha from the
#    commit row underneath survives beside a verb, where it would read as
#    if the verb were bound to that sha.
#  - The history verbs name the real branches, not placeholders: `Checkout
#    main`, `Merge main into feature (m)`, `Rebase feature onto main (r)`,
#    `Cherry-pick <sha7> (o)`, `Revert <sha7>`, `Reset feature to here,
#    mixed`/`, hard`, `Delete branch main`. `feature` is the branch
#    checked out, `main` is the row under the cursor.
#  - No verb names the branch you are standing on where git would refuse
#    it: there is no `Checkout feature` and no `Delete branch feature`.
#  - A trailing `(key)` means one thing everywhere in the menu: that
#    letter is live right now, so next time you can skip the menu. Only
#    `Merge`, `Rebase` and `Cherry-pick` carry one, because only `m`, `r`
#    and `o` (M7) exist. A
#    qualifier that is not a key never wears that shape — hence `Reset
#    …, mixed`, not `(mixed)` (`docs/design/02-keymap.md` §2.1).
#  - Choosing any of them opens a picture, not a write (PROMPT.md §1.7).
#  - The marker column has settled: `feature`'s tip carries the radar's
#    muted `ⓘ`. Earlier captures were taken before the radar
#    answered and the column was blank — that was the transient, not
#    this. What the finding says is not part of this picture.
#  - At 80 columns — the narrow end — the menu still fits
#    inside the graph pane rather than running off it.
#

docs/shots/m5-ui-credential-over-graph-160x48.txt
what right looks like: Capture header "What right looks like here" (ADR-0040): the credential prompt clears the full-width band it stands on (the graph above and the footer below stay), titled `Credentials — 127.0.0.1:8443`, with a masked field of a fixed 8 glyphs, never the typed length, and no plaintext anywhere in the capture. The border rule no longer runs into the title or the key hints.
================================================================================

# m5-ui-credential-over-graph-160x48.txt: 160x48, drawn by
# `view::view` from a real AppState — the same repository and the
# same running push as m5-ui-confirm-over-graph-160x48.txt, with
# git's password question opened on the job the confirm started
# (`update::credential::credential_needed`, the entry point
# `Progress::CredentialNeeded` uses) and a seven-character password
# typed into it
# (crates/graft/tests/it/two_boxes_over_content.rs,
# capture_two_boxes_over_real_content_for_docs_shots, asserted).
# The host in the question is pinned to `127.0.0.1:8443`: a real HTTP
# fixture is served on a port the OS picks, and a capture whose title
# changed every run could not be diffed. Not a pty capture — no
# colour attributes, CLAUDE.md rule 5.
#
# **What right looks like here** (ADR-0040): the opposite outcome,
# from the same rule. The prompt **clears the band it stands on**,
# full width, at every width. Two reasons, either sufficient: at 80
# its right border landed inside the short-SHA column and left four-
# character tails standing against it, reading as identifiers that
# are not; and nothing behind a modal password question serves the
# task — the prompt's own border says which push is waiting
# (`esc cancel the push`); the bottom row is its keys (m6-conflicts/69).
#
# It clears **the band**, not the screen: the graph above it and the
# footer below it stay. So there is nothing beside the prompt in the
# rows it occupies, and that is the picture, not an omission — the
# writer asserts it before writing this file, and a change of heart
# fails there rather than going stale here.
#
# The border's rule no longer runs into the title or the key hints:
# `Credentials — 127.0.0.1:8443───` read as part of the host. The
# prompt's private copy of `frame_box::border_row` is gone and the
# four bordered surfaces share one implementation (ADR-0040).
#
# ADR-0038 §2 is unchanged and holds here: the field draws a fixed
# 8 mask glyphs whatever was typed, never the typed length, and the
# plaintext is in no row of this file (the writer asserts both).

== git's password question, over the push it belongs to ==

 graft /code/api  200 commits
◆ ▏ⓘ [◆ main ↑1] Commit 200                                                                                                                      GF 2d   d5ae5fd

docs/shots/m5-ui-credential-over-graph-80x24.txt
what right looks like: Capture header "What right looks like here" (ADR-0040): the credential prompt clears the full-width band it stands on (the graph above and the footer below stay), titled `Credentials — 127.0.0.1:8443`, with a masked field of a fixed 8 glyphs, never the typed length, and no plaintext anywhere in the capture. The border rule no longer runs into the title or the key hints.
================================================================================

# m5-ui-credential-over-graph-80x24.txt: 80x24, drawn by
# `view::view` from a real AppState — the same repository and the
# same running push as m5-ui-confirm-over-graph-80x24.txt, with
# git's password question opened on the job the confirm started
# (`update::credential::credential_needed`, the entry point
# `Progress::CredentialNeeded` uses) and a seven-character password
# typed into it
# (crates/graft/tests/it/two_boxes_over_content.rs,
# capture_two_boxes_over_real_content_for_docs_shots, asserted).
# The host in the question is pinned to `127.0.0.1:8443`: a real HTTP
# fixture is served on a port the OS picks, and a capture whose title
# changed every run could not be diffed. Not a pty capture — no
# colour attributes, CLAUDE.md rule 5.
#
# **What right looks like here** (ADR-0040): the opposite outcome,
# from the same rule. The prompt **clears the band it stands on**,
# full width, at every width. Two reasons, either sufficient: at 80
# its right border landed inside the short-SHA column and left four-
# character tails standing against it, reading as identifiers that
# are not; and nothing behind a modal password question serves the
# task — the prompt's own border says which push is waiting
# (`esc cancel the push`); the bottom row is its keys (m6-conflicts/69).
#
# It clears **the band**, not the screen: the graph above it and the
# footer below it stay. So there is nothing beside the prompt in the
# rows it occupies, and that is the picture, not an omission — the
# writer asserts it before writing this file, and a change of heart
# fails there rather than going stale here.
#
# The border's rule no longer runs into the title or the key hints:
# `Credentials — 127.0.0.1:8443───` read as part of the host. The
# prompt's private copy of `frame_box::border_row` is gone and the
# four bordered surfaces share one implementation (ADR-0040).
#
# ADR-0038 §2 is unchanged and holds here: the field draws a fixed
# 8 mask glyphs whatever was typed, never the typed length, and the
# plaintext is in no row of this file (the writer asserts both).

== git's password question, over the push it belongs to ==

# m5-ui-dragging-160x48.txt: drawn by `view::view` from a real
# AppState over a real repository (`main` three commits, `feature` forked off
# the first with two of its own, `feature` checked out), opened over the real
# job pool, `feature`'s badge pressed and dragged onto `main`'s row — the
# button is **still down**, two real mouse events through `update`, no release
# (crates/graft/tests/it/name_and_drag.rs, capture_a_drag_in_flight_for_docs_shots).
# A golden snapshot: that test fails if the frame drifts. Regenerate on
# purpose with GRAFT_UPDATE_SHOTS=1. The terminal is ratatui's TestBackend, so
# this is a character grid with no colour attributes in it — CLAUDE.md rule 5,
# colour ships unverified, and the raised background on two of these rows is
# **not** in this file. The three marks below are shapes for exactly that
# reason.
#
# What right looks like:
#  - `main`'s row carries `▸` in the marker column: this is where the badge
#    would land.
#  - The row `feature`'s badge came off is faded — the badge is in the air,
#    not on that row. Here that is also the row the cursor is on (the badge
#    was picked up from under it), so the fade replaces the cursor's own
#    `▏`: one row, one state. Drag from a row the cursor is not on and both
#    marks are drawn, `▏` and `▸`, on different rows.
#  - The footer reads `release drop on a row  esc cancel`.
#  - Nothing else has moved: no menu, no box, the graph unchanged.

================================================================================

# m5-ui-drop-menu-160x48.txt: drawn by `view::view` from a real
# AppState over a real repository (`main` three commits, `feature` forked off
# the first with two of its own, `feature` checked out), opened over the real
# job pool, `feature`'s badge pressed, dragged onto `main`'s row and released
# there — three real mouse events through `update`
# (crates/graft/tests/it/name_and_drag.rs, capture_the_drop_menu_for_docs_shots).
# A golden snapshot: that test fails if the frame drifts. Regenerate on
# purpose with GRAFT_UPDATE_SHOTS=1. The terminal is ratatui's TestBackend, so
# this is a character grid with no colour attributes in it — CLAUDE.md rule 5,
# colour ships unverified.
#
# What right looks like:
#  - A title row above the verbs reads `feature → main`, so the menu says what
#    went where without the user having to remember the gesture.
#  - Every verb names both branches, never `this` or `that`.
#  - A verb that cannot run is dim and carries its reason after ` — `.
#  - `Reset` names its mode after a comma (`, mixed` / `, hard`), never in
#    parentheses: a trailing `(k)` is reserved for a live key.
#  - The menu sits inside the graph pane rather than running off it, and
#    covers whole columns of the graph (ADR-0040) — no half-covered column
#    shows beside it.
#  - The menu opens directly under `main`'s row — the row the badge landed
#    on, which is still readable above it.
#

docs/shots/m5-ui-ghost-rows.txt
what right looks like: Capture header "What right looks like": real commits above are solid lines with real node shapes (●/◉/◇); the ghost slice below is parents clipped at the preview's edge, drawn with a hollow anchor (○, or ◎ for a ghost merge) and dashed edges (┊/┈) — no ghost row may look like a real parent. When the preview owns the row every edge on the ghost rows dashes; when a real lane runs through, only the anchor's own lane is the preview's and the real branch keeps its solid glyph and colour.
================================================================================

# docs/shots/m5-ui-ghost-rows.txt — ghost anchor vs real parent
#
# What right looks like: the top rows are real commits — solid
# lines, the node's real shape (●/◉/◇). The bottom two rows are the
# ghost slice: parents clipped at the preview's edge, drawn with a
# hollow anchor (○, or ◎ for a ghost merge) and dashed edges (┊/┈).
# No ghost row may look like a real parent at either tier.
#
# Two cases, because which lanes belong to the preview is the
# caller's to say:
#  - "the preview owns the row": every edge on the ghost rows is
#    the preview's, so every edge dashes.
#  - "a real lane runs through": only the anchor's own lane is the
#    preview's. The real branch crossing those rows keeps its solid
#    glyph and its colour — DESIGN.md §1.7's `┊│┊●b┈`, so the
#    before and the after read as one picture, not two graphs.
#
# Colour is unverified by this capture (CLAUDE.md rule 5) — the
# shape difference is what a colourless terminal, and NO_COLOR,
# rely on.

=== the preview owns the row — Unicode tier, 8 cols ===
◉─╮     
│ ●     
●─╯     
◉─╮     
┊ ○     
○┈╯     

=== the preview owns the row — ASCII tier, 8 cols ===
*-\     
| *     
*-/     
*-\     
: o     
o./     

=== a real lane runs through — Unicode tier, 8 cols ===
◉─╮     
│ ●     
●─╯     
◉─╮     
│ ○     
○─╯     

=== a real lane runs through — ASCII tier, 8 cols ===
*-\     
| *     
*-/     
*-\     
| o     
o-/

docs/shots/m5-ui-preview-box.txt
what right looks like: Capture header "What right looks like": the box is docked to the bottom of the screen at its own height, its own footer (`←→ choose  ⏎ act  esc cancel`) on its last row with the screen's own footer row untouched below it; every interior row is bordered (`│ … │`) and every choice is bracketed, with `▸` on the cursor's choice resting on `Cancel`. While planning, the plan's lines read `predicting…` instead of a plan not yet computed; below 40x12 the box collapses to one row: `preview needs 40x12 · esc closes`.
================================================================================

# docs/shots/m5-ui-preview-box.txt — Ghost Preview box
#
# What right looks like: the box is docked to the bottom of the
# screen at its own height, its own footer ("←→ choose  ⏎ act  esc
# cancel") on its last row and the screen's own footer row below it
# untouched. Every row between the two borders is a `│ … │` row —
# there is no hole in the box at any size. Every choice is
# bracketed; the cursor's carries `▸` and rests on `Cancel`
# (ADR-0038 §1). While `planning` is set, the plan's lines are
# replaced by `predicting…` — no plan is shown before it is
# computed. Below 40x12 of screen the box is one row: "preview
# needs 40x12 · esc closes".
#
# Every row of the screen is printed, blank ones included. Colour
# is unverified: this is a character grid (CLAUDE.md rule 5), so
# the reversed cursor button cannot be judged here — the `▸` can.

=== ready, docked in 80x24 ===

# m5-ui-preview-rebase-160x48.txt: 160x48, drawn by `view::view`
# from a real AppState — a real repository (`main` three commits, `feature`
# forked off the first with two of its own, `feature` checked out), opened
# over the real job pool, cursor moved to `main`'s row and `r` pressed
# through `update`, then the real `graft_ops::preview::plan` run
# (crates/graft/tests/it/preview.rs, capture_preview_for_docs_shots,
# asserted). Not a pty capture: the terminal is ratatui's TestBackend, so
# this is a character grid with no colour attributes in it — CLAUDE.md rule
# 5, colour ships unverified. The scratch repository's temporary path is
# replaced by `/code/api`; nothing else is touched.
#
# What right looks like:
#  - Two ghost rows for the commits the rebase would replay: a hollow node
#    glyph, dashed edges, and `—` in place of a short sha and an age,
#    because those commits do not exist yet.
#  - `feature`'s badge has left its old row and sits on the newest ghost —
#    the picture shows where the branch *would* be, not where it is.
#  - The box is docked to the bottom of the graph, above the footer row, and
#    it is a box: every interior row bordered, nothing drawn in a hole.
#  - The box names what happens in the plan's own words, shows the real
#    `git rebase …` line it would run, and offers `[ Cancel ]` first with
#    the cursor on it (ADR-0038 §1: the safe choice is where the cursor
#    rests).
#  - The rows behind the box are the picture, not the live graph, and the
#    box covers rows the graph never drew — no real row is hidden by it.
#

# m5-ui-preview-scrolled-160x48.txt: 160x48, drawn by `view::view`
# from a real AppState. A real repository: `old-release` cut at the base,
# three commits on `main`, `topic` forked off its tip with two of its own,
# and `redesign` — sixty commits newer than all of them — pushing
# `old-release` far down the graph. Opened over the real job pool, the
# cursor walked down to `old-release`'s row with `j` **at this screen
# size** (so the viewport really is scrolled: `history.top` is 30 here,
# not 0 — it differs by screen, which is why each capture has its own
# session and its own number), then `r` pressed through `update` and the
# real `graft_ops::preview::plan` run (crates/graft/tests/it/preview.rs,
# capture_scrolled_preview_for_docs_shots, asserted). Not a pty capture:
# ratatui's TestBackend, a character grid with no colour attributes in it
# — CLAUDE.md rule 5, colour ships unverified. The scratch repository's
# temporary path is replaced by `/code/api`; nothing else is touched.
#
# What right looks like:
#  - The rows on screen are the rows the user was looking at. `cut release
#    1.0` — the row the cursor was on when `r` was pressed — is visible,
#    and the newest commits (`redesign step 59` and its neighbours, a
#    screen or more above) are **not**. Before ticket 17 this capture
#    showed exactly those rows instead, and the user's own were off-screen.
#  - The five predicted rows sit right above `cut release 1.0`: hollow
#    node glyphs, dashed edges, `—` in place of a short sha and an age.
#    They are `main`'s three commits and `topic`'s two, replayed.
#  - **An `after rebase` label on its own row above them**, and the box's
#    ref line reads `topic e7e39a7 → 5 new commits`. Before m5/20 the
#    block had no label and no separator, the five subjects were word for
#    word the five real rows above them, and the line said `→ ghost`
#    — a word the interface never defines. The first available reading
#    was `these commits are in my history twice`, which is the confusion
#    M2 exists to prevent.
#  - `topic`'s badge has left its own row and sits on the newest of them,
#    directly under the label.
#  - The highlighted row is `cut release 1.0`: the commit the key was
#    pressed on, not whichever row happens to sit where the box's choice
#    cursor points. (Highlight is a colour, so the grid cannot show it —
#    unverified by construction, rule 5.)
#  - The box is docked above the footer, every interior row bordered, and
#    `[ Cancel ]` comes first with the cursor on it (ADR-0038 §1).
#

docs/shots/m5-ui-preview-time-machine-160x48.txt
what right looks like: Capture header "What right looks like": the journal browser is replaced in place by the preview box (`Esc` restores it on the same row); the box states what reverting to before that entry would do in the plan's own words, with no `git …` line since a revert is Graft's own step-by-step restore, and `[ Cancel ]` is first with the cursor on it.
================================================================================

# m5-ui-preview-time-machine-160x48.txt: 160x48, drawn by
# `view::view` from a real AppState. A real repository with one commit and
# three files staged one at a time through the changes pane (three journal
# entries), then `J`, `j`, `j`, `Enter` on the oldest of the three, through
# `update` over the real job pool, then the real
# `graft_ops::preview::plan_revert_to` run
# (crates/graft/tests/it/preview.rs, capture_time_machine_for_docs_shots,
# asserted). Not a pty capture: ratatui's TestBackend, a character grid
# with no colour attributes — CLAUDE.md rule 5, colour ships
# unverified. The scratch repository's temporary path is replaced by
# `/code/api`, and the base commit's id — invented by this run, so
# different every time — is zeroed to `0000000`; nothing else is
# touched.
#
# What right looks like:
#  - The journal browser is gone and the preview box is in its place. `Esc`
#    puts the browser back on the same row.
#  - The box says what reverting to before that entry would do, in the
#    plan's own words — how many steps, and what the index and working
#    tree would be. **No `git …` line:** a revert is `graft`'s own
#    restore, step by step, not a git command anyone could type, and
#    `plan_revert_to` returns no commands (review 08 Minor 6 — this
#    header used to ask the reader to look for one).
#  - `[ Cancel ]` is first and the cursor rests on it.
#  - Nothing has run: this picture is a read.
#

 graft /code/api  4 commits
◆ ▏  [◆ main] add the base                                                                                                                       GT now  0000000
●    Correct the note                                                                                                                            GF 7y   a82960b
●    Add the first note                                                                                                                          GF 7y   fadcfb3
◇    Add a readme                                                                                                                                GF 7y   64ded19

docs/shots/m5-ui-undo-after-push-80x24.txt
what right looks like: Capture header "What right looks like": the first box names the remote side, saying in words that undo is local only and that re-pushing the old tip rewrites a branch others may have pulled, with three answers and `Cancel` first; choosing `[ Re-push old tip ]` opens a second box — the ordinary push confirm — showing the command with `--force-with-lease`, never a bare `--force`, before anything is sent. Known cosmetic defect of this capture, not the app: the header row shows the raw scratch path (e.g. `<scratch_______________________________>…`) instead of the substituted `/code/api` — don't file it twice.
================================================================================

# m5-ui-undo-after-push-80x24.txt: 80x24, drawn by `view::view` from a
# real AppState — a scratch repository pushed to a `file://` bare,
# then `u` (crates/graft/tests/it/remote_by_key.rs,
# capture_undo_after_push_for_docs_shots, asserted). Not a pty
# capture: the terminal is ratatui's TestBackend, so this is a
# character grid with no colour attributes in it — CLAUDE.md rule 5,
# colour ships unverified.
#
# Why: `u` undoes your local branch. A push has already sent that work
# somewhere others can pull. Undoing silently would leave the two
# disagreeing with no word about it (ADR-0038 §4).
#
# What right looks like:
#  - **The first box names the remote side** and says in words that
#    undo is local only, and that re-pushing the old tip rewrites a
#    branch others may have pulled. Three answers, `Cancel` first.
#  - **Re-push asks a second time.** Choosing `[ Re-push old tip ]`
#    does not push: it opens the ordinary push confirm, showing the
#    exact command. Two deliberate answers before a remote branch is
#    rewritten.
#  - **The command line says `--force-with-lease`**, never a bare
#    `--force`. At 80 columns the box is narrower than the full
#    command, so the tail is clipped — the same clipping the M4 lease
#    box already takes (noted in the ticket; the fix is in graft-ops).
#  - Your local branch keeps every commit it has: re-push moves the
#    remote back, not you.
#
# The `to push` commit is made by this test moments before the frame is
# drawn, so its id is new on every run. It is zeroed to `0000000` in
# this file, at the width it was drawn at, so the capture can be
# compared to the code. Nothing else here is normalised.
